notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (customer support automation) evaluating Redwood Hosted API for chat/agent workload with a view to Dedicated for production. Current plan: POC on Hosted to validate streaming & tool-calling SLOs, then move to Dedicated for stable capacity and SLAs. Reason for migration: incumbent (IncumbentAI) has had repeated latency regressions and broken streams for our high-concurrency chat flows; product team reports increased user complaints. Quote from Head of Product: 'streams are stalling mid-response; function calls time out under load'

Key requirements/targets:
- Workload: real-time chat + autonomous agent orchestrations (tool calls to search, ticketing APIs).
- Concurrency target: 150-250 concurrent conversations during peak; expected steady-state ~80 convos.
- Token profile: avg conversation length 600-1,200 tokens; bursts up to 3k tokens for deep troubleshooting flows.
- Latency SLOs: token-stream pacing 95th <200ms; first-byte (start of response) <250ms; function-call end-to-end <600ms.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget; looking for predictable committed pricing once traffic stabilizes.
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2, audit logs, envelope encryption (KMS), optional EU data residency for EU customers.

Benchmark summary (redwood vs incumbent) - internal POC run 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-05:
- Test harness: replay of 10k representative conversations (mix of short troubleshooting and long agent flows), 200 concurrent workers, streaming enabled, function-calls exercised on 30% of requests.
- Redwood Hosted (streaming): median first-byte 95ms, 95th first-byte 210ms, token-to-token steady-state median 60ms, 95th 180ms. Streams remained stable with <0.5% aborted streams. Function-call round trip median 310ms.
- IncumbentAI (streaming): median first-byte 340ms, 95th 780ms, token-to-token 95th 420ms, stream aborts ~4.8%. Function-call round trip median 940ms and several timeouts at load.
- Notes: Redwood's continuous batching + KV caching reduced tail spikes; incumbent suffered from cold-start and backpressure during bursts. Subjective: engineers reported noticeably smoother token arrival from Redwood; less jitter.

POC outcomes and asks:
- Product team is satisfied with Redwood streaming stability and tool-calling latency; primary remaining asks are: formal Dedicated pricing for committed capacity, SOC2 evidence & DPA, and confirmation of EU residency options. Engineering requests a 4-week Dedicated pilot to validate production traffic patterns (autoscaling, cold-starts, burst behavior).

- Data residency: will require confirmation and potential routing rules for EU customer subset.
